_note: How much research each run does. Research runs every 15 minutes and starts as many researchers as the queue needs, up to sweep.researchers (the cap on usage); an empty queue starts none. Gap searchers: sweep.gap_workers every sweep.gap_every_minutes, plus sweep.gap_spare_workers while the 5-hour usage window is under sweep.gap_spare_below_pct of its estimate, none when usage is tight (measured 2026-11-19/20: 122 gap runs added 11 events, 91% added nothing, $3.58 per event against $0.95 for a researcher). The backlog desk only acts when more than backlog.leave_for_sweep stories are waiting. The editor job may move these by at most a quarter a week; the owner can set them to anything. headless true (owner, 2026-11-19): every AI job runs as one scripts/run-job.mjs call in swarm phases (plan, claim leases, work, check, retry, commit, report); a job whose workers cannot read the web here falls back to subagents. sweep.review_workers: every research run also starts up to this many reviewers (continuous second review), each with up to review.events_per_reviewer events; with two or more, reviewer 1 takes the events that started waiting most recently (so an event published in one cycle is reviewed in the next) and the others the oldest first, and reviewers start alternating with researchers instead of after them (scripts/review.mjs planBatches, scripts/run-job.mjs mixWork). Raised from 2 to 4 on 2026-11-20: published -> second review was p50 36 min, p90 1099 min against the 15-minute target. The review desk catches the rest. flow: research is one continuous loop (run-job.mjs flow): collect, research new stories and review earlier events in parallel, commit, repeat every min_cycle_minutes or as soon as a cycle ends; it lives `minutes` and the research schedules restart it. flow.update_workers: each cycle also starts up to this many updaters on published events with new reporting (scripts/updates.mjs); flow.followup_every_minutes: how often the loop also runs the follow-up desk on developing and claimed events. flow.grid_workers / flow.grid_per_worker: each cycle also runs scripts/grid.mjs collect, then starts up to grid_workers grid researchers (role grid) on the biggest grid outages that need a cause, grid_per_worker incidents each (scripts/grid-desk.mjs plan and apply; 0 turns it off). flow.outage_workers / flow.outage_per_worker: each cycle also starts up to outage_workers outage checkers (role outage) on unchecked outage reports (news-reported power outages, IODA internet disruptions, status-page outages), outage_per_worker each (scripts/outage-desk.mjs plan and apply; 0 turns it off; off when usage is tight or stopped). outage_desk: the desk's thresholds (see its own _note). flow.claims_workers / flow.claims_per_worker: each cycle also starts up to claims_workers claims checkers (role claims) on ransomware and extortion leak-site claims, most notable victim first, claims_per_worker each (scripts/claims-desk.mjs plan and apply; 0 turns it off; on in every usage level except stop). claims_desk: the desk's windows (see its own _note). flow.idle_backoff_minutes: how long the loop waits after 0, 1, 2+ idle cycles in a row; collection keeps min_cycle_minutes during a longer wait and work found starts the next cycle at once. usage_budget: see its own _note (scripts/lib/usage.mjs).

outage_desk._note: The outage desk (scripts/outage-desk.mjs): which unchecked outage reports an outage checker verifies. recheck_hours: a report (or another report with the same key, e.g. the same country's IODA signal on another day) checked this recently is not checked again; max_tries: a not_confirmed report is checked again after recheck_hours until this many tries; confirmed and cyber_lead are final. News-reported power outages (not taken by the grid desk, no operator incident open in that country): a stated figure of news_min_figure or more, news_min_publishers or more publishers, a nationwide headline or a cyber headline; a stated figure below news_skip_below is left out unless a headline speaks of a cyberattack. IODA: a country score of ioda_min_score or more, or ioda_min_signals or more independent measurements. Status pages: leads of kind status from the last status_hours. A country or provider with a category outage event in the last event_days days is already on the map. The owner may change any of these.

claims_desk._note: The claims desk (scripts/claims-desk.mjs): which leak-site claims (leads of kind claim) a claims checker verifies. window_days: claims read from the leads of this many days. new_hours: a claim never checked is taken only while it is younger than this. recheck_hours: an unconfirmed claim is checked again after this many hours, until max_tries; confirmed_by_victim, reported, denied and not_found are final (the follow-up desk takes a claimed event from there). match_days: a claim whose victim is named by an incident event dated within this many days is already on the map and is left out. Masked victims (private people) are never queued. The owner may change any of these.

usage_budget._note: The Max plan has no dollar limit but a 5-hour and a weekly usage window, and it does not publish them. These are estimates (scripts/lib/usage.mjs reads data/usage/*.jsonl, headless workers only; the ops and interactive sessions use the same plan and are not counted, so keep a margin). Derived 2026-11-20 from 26.6 hours of the usage log (2026-11-19 04:35 to 11-20 07:13), no limit hit in that time: peak rolling 5 hours 86.0 M tokens and $40.05 (19 Nov 17:47 to 22:47, while two loops ran at once), x 1.5 = window_tokens and window_cost. The log holds less than a week, so the weekly figures are the peak rolling 24 hours (319.1 M tokens, $152.25) x 7 x 1.5. Levels: tight at tight_pct of either window (the loop runs only researchers on incidents and exploited flaws and reviewers past 20 minutes; the jobs in tight_skip_jobs wait), stop at stop_pct of the 5-hour window or on a real limit hit (no workers until the reset time the error gives, else limit_backoff_minutes). The weekly estimate never stops the loop by itself. Re-derive these once a full week of the log exists (node scripts/lib/usage.mjs prints the current level and the peaks).
